channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: OPEC+ likely to maintain current oil production levels in November, says Bloomberg
item.description: Seven leading OPEC+ countries, including Russia, Saudi Arabia, and Kazakhstan, are expected to keep their current oil production targets unchanged in November, according to Bloomberg sources. The existing roadmap is set to be approved at the upcoming ministerial meeting scheduled for October 4, 2026. The alliance previously decided to maintain October's output at September levels.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Pledges 1% of GDP for Science and AI Development
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev announced plans to increase national spending on scientific research to 1% of GDP. He highlighted artificial intelligence, the launch of the alem.cloud supercomputer cluster, and the AI-Sana training program. Tokayev invited German companies to use Kazakhstan as a testing ground for Industry 4.0 technologies.

item.title: Turkistan Region Harvests Over 90 Percent of Crops, Government Reviews Campaign
item.description: A government meeting chaired by Prime Minister Oljas Bektenov reviewed the progress of the harvest campaign and autumn field work in the Turkistan region. Over 90% of crops have been harvested from 920,100 hectares, an increase of 9,000 hectares from last year. Priority was given to crop diversification and efficient water resource use.

item.title: Uzbekistan Ranks 77th in Global Innovation Index, Improving by Two Positions
item.description: Uzbekistan has climbed to 77th place out of 139 countries in the 2026 Global Innovation Index, a two-position improvement from the previous year. The country secured 8th place among 36 low and middle-income nations and 4th in the Central and South Asia region. The index is compiled by WIPO and Portulans Institute.

item.title: Uzbek-Belarus Inter-Parliamentary Forum Opens in Khiva to Boost Strategic Partnership
item.description: The fourth Uzbek-Belarus Inter-Parliamentary Forum, themed 'Strategic Partnership: Developing Inter-Parliamentary Dialogue, New Tasks and Prospects for Cooperation,' has commenced in Khiva. The event aims to further develop dialogue, identify new areas of cooperation, and strengthen partnerships. A business forum for women entrepreneurs and a national product exhibition are also planned.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Proposes Educational Exchange Program with Germany
item.description: During his visit to Germany, President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev met with university rectors and research institute heads. He proposed an educational exchange program to strengthen academic ties, noting current collaborations between 45 Kazakh and 100 German universities. Kazakhstan aims to attract international university standards domestically, increasing foreign student numbers to 100,000 by 2029.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Clarifies Stance on Ukraine Conflict Freeze
item.description: During a press briefing in Germany, President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev clarified his previous statement on freezing the conflict between Russia and Ukraine. He reiterated Kazakhstan's commitment to the UN Charter and respect for territorial integrity. Tokayev emphasized the need for diplomatic negotiations, stating that an immediate cessation of hostilities might be unrealistic.

item.title: Kazakhstan President Tokayev Announces Significant Breakthrough in Relations with Germany
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev stated that new strategic agreements have been reached with Germany, elevating bilateral relations to a new level. He expressed optimism for future cooperation and invited German Chancellor Merz for a state visit next year.

item.title: Critique of Resistance Commander's Public Videos Raises Concerns Over Security Risks
item.description: The repeated release of videos showing resistance commander Saleh Mohammad Rigestani's activities in the Hindu Kush foothills has drawn criticism. Concerns are raised about the security implications of revealing operational details to the Taliban, potentially endangering resistance members.

item.title: Afghanistan's Banking Restrictions Force Reliance on Exchange Shops and Hawala Systems
item.description: Despite operational banks, Afghan citizens and traders prefer money exchange shops and hawala due to withdrawal limits, complex procedures, delays, and distrust. Exchange services offer faster settlements and easier access, with some shops providing support after financial losses, unlike banks.

item.title: Kazakh President and German Chancellor Discuss Cooperation and Future Agreements
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev and German Chancellor Olaf Scholz held discussions, with Tokayev expressing high regard for bilateral cooperation and optimism for new agreements. He invited Scholz for a state visit next year. Tokayev also commented on the situation in Russia and a temporary ceasefire in Ukraine.

item.title: Central Asian common market could replace Eurasian Economic Union, analysis suggests
item.description: An analysis argues the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU) has failed to deliver on its promises of free trade and labor movement. Russia's geopolitical actions and focus on Ukraine have undermined the bloc, leading to calls for a new Central Asian common market.

item.title: Two Taliban members arrested for beating children in Spin Boldak
item.description: Taliban security forces in Kandahar confirmed the arrest of two armed members accused of beating and torturing children in Spin Boldak district. A source stated the individuals detained at least 12 children, accusing them of smuggling goods. A video of the incident has drawn widespread condemnation.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Germany Sign Commercial Agreements Worth $2 Billion
item.description: Kazakhstan and Germany have signed over 30 commercial documents valued at approximately $2 billion following negotiations in Berlin. President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev stated that the implementation of these contracts will strengthen economic cooperation between the two nations. Germany is considered a reliable strategic partner in Europe.

item.title: Official Dismissed Over Tender Violations in Atyrau Region's Construction Department
item.description: The head of the construction department in the Kurmangazy district has been dismissed due to tender violations. The department purchased 30 apartments with defects, and the head was aware of issues before the procurement. Another official received a warning for similar violations in the Kyzylkoginsky district.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Iran Presidents Hold Phone Conversation on Cooperation
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev spoke with Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian by phone. They congratulated each other and discussed strengthening bilateral cooperation in trade, economy, investment, and cultural-humanitarian spheres. Regional issues and upcoming events were also on the agenda.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev and Friedrich Merz Hold Joint Press Conference
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev met with Friedrich Merz, emphasizing strengthened bilateral ties and Germany's significant global influence. Tokayev congratulated Germany on its Day of Unity and highlighted the 35th anniversary of diplomatic relations, noting progress in trade, investment, and cultural exchange.

item.title: Student Protests Erupt Across France Over Education System Concerns
item.description: Protests over education and public service issues intensified in France, spreading nationwide. Clashes between students and police occurred in Lille, Bordeaux, Rennes, Nantes, Marseille, and Paris. Students voiced dissatisfaction with long school hours and demanding schedules, leading to arrests and injuries.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Russia Discuss Further Development of Relations
item.description: Uzbekistan's Foreign Minister Bakhtiyor Saidov met with the Russian Ambassador to Uzbekistan, Alexey Yerkhov. They discussed bilateral relations, the comprehensive strategic partnership, and upcoming contacts. Both sides expressed readiness to continue close cooperation to further develop multifaceted ties between the two countries.

item.title: AIIB May Finance Infrastructure Projects in Uzbekistan Up to $5 Billion
item.description: Uzbekistan and the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) signed an updated investment program for 2026-2029. Under the program, the AIIB may finance infrastructure projects in Uzbekistan up to $5 billion. The agreement was signed in Doha during the AIIB's 11th annual meeting.

item.title: Kazakh President Invites German Chancellor to Visit Kazakhstan
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev invited German Chancellor Friedrich Merz for a state visit. The invitation followed talks in Berlin, where both sides affirmed their intention to strengthen cooperation and create conditions for expansion. Germany is a key trade partner and investor in Kazakhstan.

item.title: Kazakhstan President Tokayev Holds Talks with German Chancellor
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev met with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz to strengthen bilateral cooperation. They discussed expanding collaboration in industry, critical minerals, transport, digital technologies, and manufacturing. Both sides agreed to enhance interaction within international structures, including the "Central Asia – Germany" format. Trade turnover reached $4.5 billion last year.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Calls Putin Most Suitable Leader for Central Asia and Europe
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev described Russian President Vladimir Putin as the most suitable political figure for Central Asia, Europe, and the world. Tokayev expressed gratitude to Putin for understanding his stance on halting military actions and returning to negotiations, emphasizing their good personal relationship.

item.title: Afghanistan peace talks held in Pakistan with regional participation
item.description: A conference titled "Afghanistan and the Path to Peace" began in Islamabad, Pakistan, with the participation of opposition figures and regional representatives. The meeting aims to discuss Afghanistan's legitimacy crisis, terrorism risks, and pathways to peace. Concerns were raised about terrorist groups and the need for an inclusive government.

item.title: Obesity could cost Kazakhstan $28.7 billion by 2060, impacting economy
item.description: Obesity and overweight issues could cost Kazakhstan up to $28.7 billion by 2060, representing 2.9% of its GDP, according to the World Obesity Federation. In 2019, the economic damage was estimated at $3.49 billion, with indirect costs like reduced productivity and premature mortality being the largest component.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev holds talks with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev met with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz to strengthen multifaceted cooperation between Kazakhstan and Germany. They confirmed commitment to expanding bilateral ties, particularly in industry, critical minerals, transport, digital technologies, and manufacturing. Trade volume increased by 13.4% to $4.5 billion last year.

item.title: Tokayev Discusses Putin Relations and Ukraine War Freeze Proposal in Germany
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev stated in Berlin that Russian President Vladimir Putin understood his personal position on freezing the war in Ukraine. Tokayev described Putin as an outstanding statesman and the most acceptable political figure for Central Asia, Europe, and the world.

item.title: Uzbekistan Opens 445 Criminal Cases for Rape of Minors Under 14 in Four Years
item.description: Uzbekistan has initiated 445 criminal cases concerning the rape of individuals under 14 years old over the past four years. A law passed in its lower house aims to improve child protection against various forms of violence.

item.title: Construction of High-Rise Halted in Bishkek's Tunguch Microdistrict Due to Violations
item.description: Authorities have halted the construction of a nine-story building in Bishkek's Tunguch microdistrict following the discovery of multiple violations. The identified issues posed a risk to a nearby residential building's foundation and violated safety standards. The developer faces a fine.

item.title: US Completes Full Troop Withdrawal from Iraq, Ending 20-Year Military Presence
item.description: The United States is completing the withdrawal of its remaining troops from Iraq by September 30, concluding a 20-year military engagement. The departure marks the end of Operation Inherent Resolve against ISIS and allows Iran and its allies to increase influence in the region.

item.title: Iran-Taliban Ties Tested by Closure of Shiite Institutions in Kabul
item.description: Closures of Shiite-linked institutions in Kabul, including the Fatima al-Zahra Clinic and the Tebyan Center, are straining Iran's relationship with the Taliban. These closures occur despite Tehran's continued political engagement and its stated non-support for armed resistance against the Taliban administration.

item.title: Kazakhstan Proposes Expanding Partnership in Raw Materials and Energy Infrastructure with Germany
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev proposed expanding cooperation in strategic raw materials and modernizing energy infrastructure with Germany. Kazakhstan possesses 21 of the 34 raw materials recognized by the EU, and seeks investment and technology for high-value product chains. Joint projects covering exploration, extraction, processing, and manufacturing of high-tech materials are envisioned.

item.title: Tokayev and Steinmeier Participate in Kazakhstan-Germany Business Forum
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev and German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier addressed a business forum highlighting strong bilateral relations. Tokayev emphasized Germany's role as a key strategic partner and driver of economic interaction with the EU, noting shared interests in critical materials, energy, transport, agriculture, and digitalization.

item.title: Kazakhstan Ready to Launch Investment-Industrial Initiative with Germany, Says President
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev stated Kazakhstan is prepared to launch a joint investment-industrial initiative with Germany, viewing it as a bridge strengthening economic ties between Central Asia and Europe. The current joint portfolio includes 40 initiatives worth over $54 billion, with 21 projects completed. Cooperation in automation and advanced manufacturing is expanding.

item.title: Taliban reportedly torture children in Spin Boldak for alleged smuggling
item.description: Local sources report that Taliban fighters in Spin Boldak, Kandahar province, arrested and publicly beat several children accused of smuggling goods between Spin Boldak and Chaman. A video allegedly shows the torture. Sources claim the Taliban also engage in smuggling.

item.title: Six Percent of Kyrgyzstan's Population is Aged 65 and Older
item.description: Approximately six percent of Kyrgyzstan's population comprises individuals aged 65 and older, according to the National Statistical Committee. The Ministry of Labor is developing a state program for active longevity until 2030.

item.title: Taliban official meets Chinese ambassador for farewell talks on bilateral ties
item.description: Taliban Deputy Prime Minister Abdul Salam Hanafi met with Chinese Ambassador Zhao Xing in Kabul for a farewell meeting. They discussed bilateral relations and expanding economic cooperation. The ambassador expressed China's support for the Taliban at international institutions.

item.title: US allocates $5 million to Central Asia for cybersecurity development
item.description: The United States has allocated $5 million to Central Asian countries for the development of their digital sectors and cybersecurity. The announcement was made at the C5+1 conference in Astana, focusing on artificial intelligence and cyber threats.

item.title: Uzbekistan President Launches New Investment Projects in Andijan Region
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev visited Andijan region to review socio-economic progress and launch new investment projects. The region's economy grew by 8.8% in the first half of the year. 206 investment projects worth $9.4 billion were initiated, with 98 projects already completed, totaling over $2 billion in investments.

item.title: Afghanistan Journalists Center Reports Taliban Detained Around 300 Journalists Since 2021
item.description: The Afghanistan Journalists Center (AFJC) states that the Taliban have detained approximately 300 journalists and media workers since their 2021 takeover, citing non-compliance with media guidelines. The center reports widespread restrictions on media activities, leading to the suspension or closure of numerous outlets and hindering journalists' work.
